rationales: An integer never equals a string, even one with the same digits.
== between different types is allowed; it simply answers False.
Only the empty string is false; '0' is a non-empty string.
bool always returns True or False, never the original value.
or returns one of its operands, not a Boolean.
The empty string is false, so or moves on to the second operand.

q: In an if-elif-else chain, how many branches can run?
rationales: Separate if statements would test every condition; elif stops at the first true one.
Nothing forces two; with no true condition and no else, none runs.

q: When is a match statement the better choice over an elif chain?
options: When one value is compared against many possible shapes or values
When there is a single yes-or-no condition
Never; match is only for Python 3.14
rationales: A single condition is clearest as a plain if.
